text_fidelity_a:
USB Power Strip Portable Travel Charger Outlets 2.1AMP 1AMP 21W 5Foot Power Supply Cord With Universal Plug Input From 100v-240v Power Sockets USB Charger Station 4 Port 5v 1A/2.1A USB Charger (White) This is a very unique and awesome product. It wasn't listed near the beginning of my Amazon search results, so it took me a while to find it. But it's AWESOME!!!

The first thing I do when I get to a hotel room or a cruise ship cabin is to set up my charging station. We have phones, iWatches, Kindle, iPad, and rechargable power packs, so we end up having a lot of potential things to charge. Setting up the charging area is a high priority. The best place is on a table or desk, so we can spread out our rat's nest of cables and devices with easy access. However, power outlets are often in inconvenient places, especially on a cruise ship. (On cruises, in the past I would actually bring a small extension cord.)

Anyway, this super clever travel charger solves the problem. I can plug it into the wall outlet, and run the cord up onto a table or desk. It's perfect.

Actually, the 4 USB ports isn't nearly enough for us, so one of these chargers wasn't going to entirely solve my problem. Theoretically, I could use two of them, but that's overkill in the sense that I don't need long two cords. Since this charger has a wall-plug type of outlet on the charger itself, I already have regular wall power at the charger on the table. I don't need to run a second cord from a wall outlet. Therefore, I use a small 4-port USB charger without the cord, and plug that into this charger. That gives me 8 USB ports up on the table for easy access. Here's the 4-port charger without a cord that I plug into this one:
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07JH9R89T/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

I have never seen a charger with a cord like this before, and I am very impressed with how clever and useful the design is! The one problem I found was with the child protection piece inside the slots on the charger's power socket. (This is the 110V power socket on the charger.) Because of the child protection piece, it can sometimes be very hard to get something plugged into that socket. The protection piece needs to slide to the side, so you can't just push the plug straight in, like you would at a wall socket. You need to put the prongs into the slots at an angle, and pry the protection piece out of the way. It's a pain. So, if you don't need the child protection, and you intend to use that socket, you'll probably want to remove the protection piece.

Here's how to do that. The top surface is a snap-off cover. Pull it up in the middle of one of the side, and slip a little screwdriver in there to carefully pry around and pop it off. Then there's a second cover inside that isn't attached, and will almost just fall out. On the back of that second cover, you'll see the two little springs and the plastic protection piece. Pull out the springs and the protection piece, and then put it all back together.

[NOTE: Do not remove the child protection if there will be children near it, or if you have any other safety concerns about its removal. Remove it at your own discretion and your own risk. I'm not telling you to remove it. I'm just telling you how to remove it if you want to.]

Anyway, I actually went a step further. The socket seems to be designed to accept any plug in the universe, so there are a lot of extra holes and spaces (i.e. it's not just two little slits for the normal US plug). I took white electrical tape, and taped over all the extra holes and spaces on the secondary (internal) cover, leaving just the two slits open. Then after popping on the outer cover, you just see the two open slits. All the other openings are covered internally with the white electrical tape. I think it looks much better, but this is purely a cosmetic step.

At first, it seemed like the clip for the plug is on the wrong side. It's on the same side as the USB ports. If you leave the plug in the clip (and leave the cord wrapped around the charger), then rotate the plug down 90 degrees, you can plug it into a wall outlet and the charger would be flush against the wall, hanging down from the wall socket. That seemed like it should be a nice neat way of using it without extending the cord, if desired. However, you can't do that because the USB ports end up against the wall, and you can't access them. If the clip was on the opposite side, it would work fine. As it currently is, in order to use it, you need to flip it around so the USB ports are facing out. But since the plug clip is on the wrong side, the charger sticks out from the wall at an angle. At first this seemed like a design flaw. Then I read in the instructions where it specifically says you shouldn't do any charging while the cord is wrapped around it. Presumably that's a heat issue. Therefore, it is probably designed this way on purpose, to discourage you from attempting to use the charger with the cord wrapped around it.

The bottom line is that there is no design flaw. It's prefect just the way it is. And you need to unwrap the cord when you use it, which is fine with me, since having the cord extended is the best feature of this charger.

Anyway, I think this is an awesome little gadget.
text_fidelity_b: USB Power Strip Portable Travel Charger Outlets 2.1AMP 1AMP 21W 5Foot Power Supply Cord With Universal Plug Input From 100v-240v Power Sockets USB Charger Station 4 Port 5v 1A/2.1A USB Charger (White)

Toshiba N300 6TB NAS 3.5-Inch Internal Hard Drive - CMR SATA 6 GB/s 7200 RPM 128 MB Cache - HDWN160XZSTA A NAS is a great way to add storage for the whole network where everything can be reached from any system connected. It is not as simple as a USB mass storage device like a thumb drive, of course, but it addresses a completely different issue. So far, this drive has proven to be a good one, though its reliability remains to be demonstrated over the long haul.

I have the 8TB drive, and it is great for dumping huge numbers of videos, music, documents and other media needed across a small network. It is fairly fast too, so streaming video from the NAS to any given device on the network is reasonably smooth as long as the network can handle the bandwidth (keep this detail in mind if you are wanting to stream video over a slower wireless network - the lag isn’t necessarily the drive’s fault). The drive is very quiet, though not silent, and so far seems to stay acceptably cool.

I did learn that it does not work all that well in a USB drive enclosure right out of the packaging. I have an enclosure that is capable of handling drives up to 8TB so I decided to try an experiment with the drive when it first arrived. I put it in the enclosure and connected it to my Windows 10 laptop. The system saw the device, and it even saw the drive and recognized the model and serial number, but it was unable to access the drive or even format it. I had more success with my Linux system which recognized the drive and was able to access the partition table and display drive parameters. I did not repartition the drive or create a file system for my experiment though I believe it would have worked.

Time will tell if this drive will be reliable over the long haul. Based on my experience so far, it has worked out well and I have had no issues. It’s the largest drive I have worked with and can handle a LOT of data. If you need wide open spaces for your network storage solution (or you are willing to fiddle with it to get it working as a USB solution) this is a good choice.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba N300 6TB NAS 3.5-Inch Internal Hard Drive - CMR SATA 6 GB/s 7200 RPM 128 MB Cache - HDWN160XZSTA

Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Carbon Fiber Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders The Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders is even better than I was anticipating and now I must purchase a new tripod head to get the most out of this high quality photographic instrument. To maintain a stable and secure foundation for a camera, this is outstanding -- attractive, easy to assemble, sturdy, and versatile. It arrives in a very nice cardboard box with a handle, so if you're inclined to store it in the box, you have that option. Also included is a black and orange carrying case with a shoulder strap and there is a little zippered compartment near the top of the bag for the hook, included hex key, car key, flash drive, roll of film or whatever you'd like to store. A hand crank raises and lowers the center column and it moves very smoothly, not too easy and not too hard. The tripod can simply be converted for macro shots with low camera placement. For low angle photography using very wide legs, the bottom half of the center column can very easily be removed by simply unscrewing the hook and turning the bottom ring. Very smart and pretty fast, too. Having the option to attach anti slip spiked rubber feet is a great advantage in snow or sand and adds to the stability of the tripod. When the tripod arrives, the large rubber feet are snugly attached and I doubt that they will be lost when removed to use the spikes or standard rubber feet. The three sectioned legs are extremely easy to extend with a slight turn of the amply sized twist locks and each leg has clearly marked segments for perfect measuring. They can be locked at the top, another stability and security advantage, at three angles (25, 50 and 80 degrees). If desired, a camera bag or weight can be hung from the hook on the center column. The rubber foam casing at the top of each leg makes for a very comfortable feel and aid in moving the legs and carrying tripod. Although there's a little bubble level, mine was dry, so customer service is sending me a replacement level. It's small and may be obstructed when a head and large plate or camera are attached, but it's a nice little bonus nevertheless. Changing the camera screw from 1/4" to 3/8" is another simple process that takes seconds. I'm not sure if the orange anti-shock ring really does much, but it can't hurt. This carbon tripod can hold 39 pounds and it weighs around 8 pounds. It has an ample extension and I'm very satisfied with it in all regards for use in the studio as well as in the field.

UPDATE: Vanguard CS is out of this world. When they promised to send a replacement bubble level, I was politely told it would be 2-3 months before they were expected from the manufacturer. Several weeks ago, I received a padded envelope containing a brand new perfect bubble level. It's rare that follow-up isn't necessary in a situation like this, but Vanguard clearly maintained the information to fulfill this promise. If I could award another star in my review, I would!
text_fidelity_b: Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Carbon Fiber Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders

MEE audio Atlas Sky IML Graphics On-Ear Headphones with Headset Functionality [[VIDEOID:98df0cfb6b0daad3ff2eecda806c4550]] Without a doubt, these are the most beautiful headphones made today, and I suspect that while others may follow, I doubt they will come even slightly close to this stunning set.
A few years ago, HP introduced the Vivienne Tam Mini, a red floral netbook with a matching scarf and bag. The following year was a gold butterfly version, seen in the Sex in the City film.
These machines were ridiculously expensive for the specs, but you paid for the designer and design, not printed on the case, but using a process known as in-mold labeling.
They were beyond gorgeous.

When I saw these, I knew right away that it was in-mold labeling, and someone finally embraced what the 'big guys' have been slow to catch up on.
There are those of us that want a DESIGN, not just a color, that speaks to us when we choose things that are personal to us, like headphones. We don't always want it to be the version selected by the celeb du jour, either.

I also knew I HAD to have a set! It was a tough call between the clean throwback lines of the Tron-esque 'Orion' and the opposite celestial dreaming of 'Skyline', the later being the winner by a nose (ear?).

WOW! Visually, you simply can not get better. You'll want to wear them everywhere, and here is the best part, you CAN. Unlike noise-cancelling headphones, you can still hear a bit of what's going on around you. I can finally get great sound and not worry that I'm missing the doorbell/dog bark/police siren or whatever.

They are light, in a comfortable way, not a cheap way. They fit over the ear as opposed to surrounding it, so you will not get a strong bass unless you fit the band slide perfectly. Since it adjusts smoothly, no problem.
You also don't wind up looking like you're wearing a Princess Leia wig...the big donuts over each ear.

Not many of us can carry that off, right?

But back to the sound...after all, it's what's UNDER the hood that counts.
Be it my iPhone, iPad, Galaxy (phone & tablet), PC, or Mac (tech household, what can I say), the sound is consistently true. Unlike some headphones tuned to over-accentuate bass, these nail it perfectly. That means classical comes through as beautifully as techno. And speedcore/splittercore comes through as.....well, speedcore/splittercore!

Buy for the looks, keep them for your ears and brain.
text_fidelity_b: MEE audio Atlas Sky IML Graphics On-Ear Headphones with Headset Functionality

text_fidelity_a:
Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder This is a good voice recorder. Whether you need it to record your voice memos, lectures, meetings, or discretely record your favorite spy, this will surely be a recorder you'll find many uses for.

It feels very secure in your hand, and has a comfortable feel and weight. It comes with a small pouch, which is nice. The record button is easy to find my sight or feel. The volume and forward/reverse buttons are on an outer button from the record button. Play and stop on the left and index and menu are on the right.

f1 and f2 buttons are primarily used for setting mic sensitivity and voice quality. Under Mic Sensitivity you can choose: Dictate (good for personal memos), Speech recognition (turns on when it hears voice), conversation (good for interviews or conversations, auto zoom (good for large areas where there may be close up voices and far voices), and lecture (good for lectures)

You can choose either low quality at 8kbps in Mp3 format to super high quality 192kbps in mp3. There is also a wave format in 1411 kbps. The higher quality you go impacts total record time. You can add a micro SD card for adding recording time.

There are also 4 index folders labeled A thru D. These are for separating projects. There is also a folder you could place music files if you wanted this to be a mp3 player.

There is also a menu setting where the voice quality and mic sensitivity can be accessed as well as numerous other options such as splitting files, display contrast, and clearvoice (an option that improves the sound quality of the recorded voiec)

The unit comes with rechargable AA batteries that will need to be charged when you first open it. They charge with the included usb to micro USB cord. Any other micro USB cord you own will also work. Once the recorder is connected to your computer through the USB cable you can download and upload voice or mp3 and wave files.

The only thing I wish this had was different settings for each index. For instance I would have liked to set index A for lecture mode at high quality, index B for dictate at a lower quality, etc. Once you set a mic sensitivity and recording quality, they are the same for all index until you change them in settings.

Overall a great quality recorder. Great for meetings, memos, and conversations.
text_fidelity_b: Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy NX EK-GN120ZKAXAR Galaxy Wireless Smart Android 4G Camera 20.3MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 4.8-Inch LCD with 18-55mm OIS Lens (Black) My first impression upon unboxing this camera was "Wow, that feels cheap." Everything's made from unattractive plastic. The single dial on the top rear of the camera (oddly blank) feels light, spins too easily and clicking it feels mushy. The other buttons on the camera, power, movie and flash all have the same, cheap, mushy feel. The shutter button has poor tactile feel.

The camera is surprisingly heavy; for me uncomfortably, painfully, so.The back is so taken up by the huge 4.8" LCD screen that the thumb rest is too short, more of an afterthought that cause me quite a bit of discomfort during extended use. The DSLR style handgrip is quite large (perhaps too large for small hands) to accommodate the massive 4360 mAh battery.

On paper the idea of an Android OS with a 4.8" LCD screen and a big APS-C sensor sounds great but I was sadly less than impressed.

Because of the Android OS startup time from fully off to ready to shoot is a very long 23 seconds. In standby mode the camera was ready to shoot in approx. 4 seconds. The camera runs warm, very warm, even just sitting idle on a cool 50 degree day. I would worry about overheating in the summer months.

Image quality was unimpressive especially in low light. Early morning, post sunrise, images with sky and clouds were extremely grainy and noisy. Performance in full light was better but not spectacular. Auto focus was run of the mill, often seeking excessively in low light situations. High ISO performance was exceedingly poor. Past ISO 800 images were rather noisier and grainy. In auto mode the camera seemed to make poor choices for ISO and shutter speeds.

Controls. Almost every setting is accessed via the large LCD screen.

There are over twenty pre-configured shooting modes. I used several of them while checking out this camera. These selections are made from a top to bottom scrolling 'carousel' where you scroll through until you find the option you want. I found it annoying to find and stop on the mode I wanted. You're going to miss shots trying to find the mode you want.

Continuous Shooting: burst mode. Surprisingly fast.
Kids Shot: the camera plays one of three sounds to attract a child's attention and then bursts five photos.
Macro: The Galaxy NX has a surprisingly short minimum focal distance with the kit lens and the macro photos I took were among the best results I was able to get from the camera.
Rich Tone: Samsung's HDR mode. Processing time was excessive.
Panorama: This is a sweep mode, smoothly move the camera (a tripod helps) to capture up to 180°'s of view. Disappointingly the camera reduces the image size significantly in Panorama mode.
Multi Exposure: combines two or more images into one.
Drama: combines several images of a moving subject into a single image. The camera was very picky about detecting moving objects. I encountered at least a 50% fail rate trying this mode. Additionally, as with the Panorama mode the image size is greatly reduced.

The camera can also be used in manual mode. Samsung calls it 'Expert Mode'. This gives you access to the standard PASM controls. The settings are controlled by three half-circle on screen dials that I found frustratingly hard to use. Try to change one and my thick fingers would spin the wrong dial. Using Shutter Priority mode I found the processing time of 30 second exposures was a disappointing additional 30 seconds.

There are some things I did like about this camera. It's not all bad. It can produce decent images and I honestly think the majority of the limitations I experienced were due to the cheap kit lens. The 4.8" LCD is gorgeous, in the right light, I recently went back to a camera with a beautiful 3" screen and it felt small. Some of the included shooting modes are fun to play with. Connectivity via WiFi was rock solid (I wasn't able to test the 3G/4G connectivity) even in parking lots of places that offered free WiFi. There were eleven gigs of free space in internal memory. That was plenty of room for a day's shooting and testing. I never did get around to installing an SD card.

In conclusion...
I'm not really sure who this camera is aimed at. They seem to be trying to attract smart phone users with the ability to access the internet almost anywhere and instantly share you photos. But do you really need an expensive, heavy and complex large-sensor camera to post photos to Facebook and Twitter?
On the flip side I just can't see this camera being attractive to professional photographers or high end photography enthusiasts. While the inclusion of the electronic viewfinder is nice I found the all on-screen controls to be distracting and bothersome and the image quality was for the most part lackluster.

A note about durability. As I was finishing up the testing of this camera I bobbled the camera due to nerve damage and it took a spill. The height was not great, less than three feet, and the initial impact was on soil and grass. The lens came apart into numerous pieces. I was able to put the lens back together but it appears to have suffered internal damage and will not focus either automatically or manually. I accept that I caused this damage but I am very unimpressed with the durability of such an expensive camera.

I really can't recommend this camera. Three stars but barely.

A side note about Samsung's technical support that isn't reflected in my rating of this camera. Calling Samsung's support line was a complete nightmare. Audio quality was atrocious. At the end I was practically screaming to be heard. I spent close to an hour and a half on the phone speaking with seven different people. Each person I spoke to had to be told all my information, the camera's information and the reason for my call. Four times I was transferred to 'the proper department.' In the end I had a supervisor tell me, first that the camera did not exist and then, that it must be a UK version and I'd have to start all over and call their UK support line. I then contacted Samsung through their Facebook support page. It's been almost a week and they still haven't decided what to do about the camera/lens.

{Edit}
It took nearly a month of back and forth and arguing to get Samsung to agree my camera was a US version, it was under warranty and they would issue a repair ticket for it. It was shipped off at their expense, repaired surprisingly quickly and shipped back. The camera's now in working order. Only one thing marred the process. text_fidelity_a:
museeq Bluetooth Speaker,Portable Wireless Conference Speakerphone Speaker,Waterproof Shower Speaker,Enhanced Bass,Stereo Sound,Shockproof,Dustproof Outdoor Speaker with Powerbank Black Bottom Line - The speaker itself is excellent but Bluetooth can be an irritating technology.

The speaker is lightweight and even has an attached carrying strap. Unlike a lot of lightweight products though, it doesn't feel flimsy or fragile at all. Instead it has a nice, solid, durable feel to it. While I am not an audiophile, the speaker has a deep, rich sound that I really like. It does well with audiobooks, music, and videos.

The problems seem to be with Bluetooth. One major issue is that the sound stutters while using Bluetooth. It's very noticeable when playing music and very irritating when listening to audiobooks. That's happened with every Bluetooth speaker I've ever tried. A google search indicates that it's a common problem related to the amount of information the computer is trying to pump out to the speaker. There's a checklist of possible issues to go through to try to fix the problem but the stuttering seems all too common with this technology.

Another issue involves changing modes on a Bluetooth speaker. To sidestep the stuttering I plugged this speaker into my computer with a standard jack. It worked fine and the sound was good. When I unplugged it to bring the speaker into another room with me, I had to redo my audio settings. When I plugged it back in with the jack, an audiobook played just fine but there was no sound while playing videos. Again, I had to go into the audio settings and fiddle with them to be able to watch a movie. I've had similar issues with other Bluetooth speakers.

If you are a techie you may be able to resolve such things quickly and easily. The less tech adept you are, the more hassle they will be though. Myself, I'm just going to leave the speaker connected to my pc via a good old fashioned jack because I like its sound. Bluetooth? Bah, I haven't got time to bother with it.
text_fidelity_b: museeq Bluetooth Speaker,Portable Wireless Conference Speakerphone Speaker,Waterproof Shower Speaker,Enhanced Bass,Stereo Sound,Shockproof,Dustproof Outdoor Speaker with Powerbank Black

They have a really good tone once you adjust the equalizer in the software and I was surprised at how good the bass sounded. Second, the noise reduction really works. It doesn’t block out 100%, but I’d say it knocks out about 85% of room noise. It’s really appreciated in a houseful of rowdy kids and several multimedia devices running at the same time. Pass through sound works with a quick double tap. Thirdly, they fit well. They don’t fall out and are comfortable to my ears for the duration of the battery life. They include three sizes of inserts, so fitting was easy.

There is one thing I really dislike. Micro usb. It’s the reason I deducted a star from my rating. Why, oh why, does this device use micro usb for charging? Why force me to clutter up the floor with another cable? Stupid decision to forgo usb c for micro usb.

I can’t really speak for phone use or the Alexa functionality because I don’t use it. I disabled the microphones in the software. Don’t want amazon or anyone else intruding into my private life.

Over all, these are great buds; I use them everyday.

Belkin Screen Protector for Kindle Fire - 4 Pack I bought this to keep my Kindle Fire 7" screen to be free of fingerprints, and it is working fine. The transparent overlay keeps the screen safe without changing the Kindle Fire touch screen's functionality. This screen protector is helpful in keeping finger prints/ sweats/dirt off the Kindle Fire screen, and does not obstruct the screen or access to keys and ports. In the long run, this is helpful to protect the screen from nicks and scratches. These transparent screen guards are relatively thick which makes it easy to handle but it keeps the screen clear. Another plus is that it comes in a 4-pack.

Applying the overlay is easy. First clean the Kindle Fire screen with a cleaning wipe (comes with the product), peel the overlay from its backing and place it on the Kindle screen. Air bubbles get caught between the screen and screen protector, no matter how careful you are when applying, you will trap some air bubbles. I tried to smooth out with the smoothing card but don't help much. This doesn't affect the viewing of the videos, movies or reading a book on the Kindle.

text_fidelity_a:
Valkit for New iPad Pro 12.9 2017 Cover, iPad Pro 12.9 Case, Apple iPad Pro 12.9 Inch 2015 Folio Smart Folio Stand Protective Heavy Duty Rugged Armor Cases with Apple Pencil Holder, Black This is a decent lightweight case for your iPad Pro, and it’s a good value-for-your-buck. However, I wouldn’t trust this to be your ‘durable case’, say for traveling, commuting, distracting the kids. I am concerned that a fall with this case may cause significant damage, especially as the case ages. I’ve had the case for quite a few months now, and the first thing I can note is that the PVC screen cover is very loose, and needs to be carefully placed when closing it, so that it covers the screen completely. I am no longer able to use the folded screen cover for propping the tablet up anymore, because of the wear.

On a happier note, the case *IS* easy to remove, so you can use a heavier and more protective case when you need to travel. This case adds almost no weight to the tablet as well. The colored part of the PVC hasn’t scraped off or cracked either. So, as a light weight, safe-for-home case, it’s a solid 4. As an ‘all purpose’ case, I’d rate it a 3 on it’s own, or 3.5 if you’re putting it into a computer backpack with a padded chamber for it.
text_fidelity_b: Valkit for New iPad Pro 12.9 2017 Cover, iPad Pro 12.9 Case, Apple iPad Pro 12.9 Inch 2015 Folio Smart Folio Stand Protective Heavy Duty Rugged Armor Cases with Apple Pencil Holder, Black

Nitecore D4 smart Charger 2015 version with LCD Display with 12V DC Cable & 2X EdisonBright AA to D Battery Converter Spacers As for all items made by Nitecore this charger is made in china. That being said I find their products to be high quality and well constructed. This charger is no exception. The charger is a great improvement from my Nitecore I4 as I can now select charging current when charging only one AAA or low mah battery. When I say selectable I mean from 300 ma to 750 ma. This is as far as the current adjustment goes, which is fine for most needs. The current does not stay fixed at those currents as the battery charges, but it will not apply more than the selected current during the charge cycle. It will not tell the capacity of the battery like many other chargers I have seen and owned. This charger purely charges and does not discharge so if your looking for one that does look elsewhere. La Crosse makes a nice one for NiMH and NiCad. The feature to turn the screen off during charging is nice, and was one of my biggest complaints with the I4. I use it to charge every thing from AAA to 26550 batteries. When charging the larger batteries an issue arises with how many can actually fit, and when I charge 26650 batteries that is only 2.
It is a great universal charger, and with the added Li-FePO4 charging cycle it makes it an easy choice for people that need a good solid charger that works for almost everything.
If you have any more questions feel free to ask in the comments, I will try to get back within the next few days.

Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function. Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.
2) In BIOS, make sure your boot devices are in proper order.
3) In BIOS, update RAID configuration to AHCI.

After that, it is operating as expected.

text_fidelity_a:
DEWALT DXFRS800 2 Watt Heavy Duty Walkie Talkies - Waterproof, Shock Resistant, Long Range & Rechargeable Two-Way Radio with VOX My husband has a lot of use for communication on jobs he has to do in the contracting world. We have had some jobs here at the house which required walkie talkie communication. Let's see how these performed.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
HOW ARE THEY BUILT?
These walkie talkies are tough. They come with the batteries outside of the units, so you have to put them in.

HOW TO PUT BATTERIES IN
You will need a very pointed screwdriver or a small Phillips head screw driver to get the battery cover off. When you screw it back in, it is pretty sturdy.

HOW TO TURN IT ON
The on button on the top is large and easy to cold, dirty, or gloved hands to turn on and off. You can also adjust volume.

CASE?
The case snaps on and off of the units. They stay hooked to the clothes pretty well as long as you are not moving around a lot. In that case, we found them most useful to hold the walkies in the pockets with the clip.

CLARITY OF SOUND?
The clarity of sound was superb. We were doing roof work on the top of a third story and they worked great. We also had to do work about 100 ft away from the point of origin of a wiring job, so we needed that for communication to test the connections. Again, they worked great. Very clear and worked very well.

TOUGH?
These have been dropped a few times and worked very well.

RECHARGING?
The recharging unit has a place for both walkies to be charged. The plug is separate from the base that you charge in. Each receptacle has a red light on it to let you know that the walkie is charging. The plug is small so you can use it on a power strip or in the wall outlet without blocking other outlets. Recharging is fast- within the hour- and they seem to last quite a while before needing to be recharged.

CLIPS
The clips have to be removed prior to charging.

CHANNELS
The different channels we used all worked well. We did not have to use them in a very busy area with multiple walkies, however, so we did not get to test it with a lot of walkie talkie traffic happening on a huge job site.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a very sturdy set of walkie talkies which charge up quickly and last a long time, these are fantastic for contract work and any jobs that we have had to do. My husband plans to take them to his jobs as well when needed. They have a decent range to them and are easy to operate even with gloves on.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. We really love these walkie-talkies. They have been fantastic so far for all of the jobs we have had to use them for. I will update if we have anything valuable to add in the future as we continue to use them over time.
text_fidelity_b: DEWALT DXFRS800 2 Watt Heavy Duty Walkie Talkies - Waterproof, Shock Resistant, Long Range & Rechargeable Two-Way Radio with VOX

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices Got this Logitech Bluetooth adapter after a while and a bit of researching...

I wanted to connect my iPhone and iPad to my receiver in my living room so I could broadcast music throughout my house (I have speaker located in different rooms)
So I decided it came down to three options.

1. [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492-P Bluetooth Music Receiver]]
2. [[ASIN:B004VM1T5S Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices (980-000540)]]
3. [[ASIN:B0015YJOK2 Apple Airport Express MB321LL/A [NEWEST VERSION]]]

______________

Belkin

I got the Belkin Bluetooth Receiver [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492-P Bluetooth Music Receiver]] but I had complaints about range. Even though there is a fix (which requires opening it up and removing a metal piece which other reviewers have said is just added to add some weight)the range with the fix still is not up to par. The Sound quality was below par as well.

__________________
Apple Airport Express

The Apple Airport Express is unique in solving my problem as it has one major advantage... It uses the wireless network in my home to stream music to my receiver (not Bluetooth). Awesome idea and I actually ordered one. This way I could be way out of Bluetooth range (i.e. my backyard)and still control music through my iPhone or iPad through the wireless network.
The only problem with this setup (which in the end I refused to deal with) is that you can only use your iPhone or iPad as a REMOTE to control iTunes on a computer. Meaning that you need to have a computer on with the appropriate songs on at all times if you want to listen to music. Being that we have laptops only and there is no consistent computer in the house, let alone "on", and connected to the wireless network.
This could not work for me.
Second problem with this system is that you can only play iTunes. No Pandora or other music venues such as youtube etc.
And to top it all off this Apple Airport express cost $99!!(plus the use of a computer full time)

_______________________
Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices

This is very similar to the Belkin but it literally took 2 minutes to hook up and the range that I tested so far is incredible. That being said it is using Bluetooth not Wireless Network so don't expect total wireless connectivity. The Sound quality is on par with the apple but I assume that will degrade with distance to the receiver. Other wise it is perfect.

In summation I am very happy with this product at this price. I would gladly pay $100-$200 for a system like the Apple Airport express that could play all audio from my iPhone or iPad directly and didn't require me to only use my iPhone as a remote for a computer that can only play iTunes on the network.... Until a reasonable system comes out like that I think this product will do the job nicely.

Or if your so inclined you can quickly rack up a few thousand dollars setting up a Sonos System[[ASIN:B005441AJC Sonos Play:3 All-In-One Wireless Music Player With 3 Integrated Speakers (Black, NEW)]]
But My house is already wired with speakers and such and I don't feel it is worth the investment.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 900 Rechargeable Remote with Color Touch Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First let me start by saying I am an IT professional and have been a audiophile and video hobbyist for many years. Naturally I have had a lot of different audio / video equipment over the years. I had a computer hooked up to my TV long before it was in fashion. And finally, I am always looking for the next great gadget on the market. Enter the Harmony 900.

Here is my current setup in my living room:
Samsung TV HL-T5687
Sony PS3 Move
Nyko IR Adaptor for PS3 - Media Hub Slim
Roku2 XS
Onkyo TX-NR808
Sharp DVDR-VCR DV-RW340
Cable Box Motorola DVR DCH-3416
Shuttle PC with Media Center
X10 Home Automation - Various Devices

I basically use my TV as a monitor, the only cable plugged into it is the HDMI from the receiver. Hence, the Onkyo receiver does all the sound and switching between inputs.

The Harmony 900 Experience:

I did a lot of research before buying this $250.00 remote. Considering this thing is 50.00 more that my Kindle Fire and does a whole lot less, it wasn't easy pulling the trigger.

Ergonomics:
I read the good and bad reviews and decided that this one would best fit my needs. From many of the negative reviews I concluded the biggest concern was going to be dropping it and breaking the screen. It becomes very obvious why this is the minute you put it in your hand. It is very sleek and conforms well to your hand, but is as a slippery as a fresh water eel in your hand. Also due to the few contact points with any surface other than the charger, it is very easy to slide off a couch arm or get bumped off a coffee table.

That being said, the remote is very well balanced and fits nicely in the hand. The buttons are raised and easy to push. However some of the buttons are simply in the wrong spot. The volume and channel buttons should be reversed and the "Menu" button should be located down further on the remote. The fast forward and skip buttons are perfectly positioned and the skip buttons have a notable bump on them to differentiate between the two.

The screen is actually better than I thought it would be. I can make out the display with or without my (fulltime) glasses. On the down side, it is very easy to tap on the wrong display icon when moving left and right through the screens. When this happens, depending on what you accidentally pressed, it takes a while to recover and get back to what you were watching. Some things may have turned on or off and if you weren't pointing in the right direction during the errant tap, good luck getting everything synced again.

Device Support:

The Harmony 900 claims thousands of supported devices. But good luck finding some of them. Instead of having a simple model number look up, you first have to choose the type of type of device, then the manufacturer followed by the model number. The problem is some devices are not listed in the device type or seem to be randomly added to device types you would not expect them in. There is an example in the set section below.

One thing clearly missing is a simple list of all the devices. In some cases like the X-10 IR interface module listed in many of these reviews, it is no longer available. It would be great to just enter X-10 and see every device that was compatible so you could buy the right one as an interface with the Harmony. There is no way to do this. This is a glaring omission that seems very simple to correct. Heck, a downloadable PDF would be better than nothing.

But all that said, I found every device in my house in their database and I had some fairly obscure AV stuff. And as long as the device is IR, you can custom map from any remote to the Harmony, so there really isn't any IR that cant work.

Setup:

Now I wasn't bragging when I said I was an IT professional. I simply mentioned this fact so those who are technically challenged have a baseline to consider when evaluating their ability to use and set up this device. I have built servers, computers, configured high end routers and switches and oversee hundreds of devices in several locations. And it always amazes me when I get a new piece of equipment like this, how frustrated I can get in the first few minutes of using it.

As others have mentioned, you have to install the software and set up an account to use the device. All settings are done interactively and in real time through the internet. If you don't have an internet connection, don't bother with this remote. I did not use the CD but instead downloaded the latest version from the Logitech web site. I also pre downloaded the owners manual several days before the remote arrived and read it cover to cover. So by the time I had it in my hand I was fairly comfortable with how the setup process should work. The software and driver installation was very easy and there were no USB connection problems to the remote. So far painless!

After letting the remote charge for a couple of hours I started through the setup process. I had used my own version of their worksheet and had all the devices written down. The first thing to note, again as other have mentioned is the Sony PS3 requires an add-on device to translate the IR to the Sony's native RF. Although Logitech sells such a device for almost 100.00, I already had a Nyko Media Hub for the PS3. It doesn't have all the functions of the Logitech, but it was only $17.00 and does all I need. And best of all, the Harmony 900 has the Nyko in it's database. The Roku2 XS is mysteriously placed in the DVD section and if I hadn't read some of these reviews I would not have known that. All the other devices mentioned above were in the database and all were added without an issue.

Once all the devices were added the software prompts you to add activities. Activities are the heart of the 900's functionality. However you must understand the concept of "Activities" and how they work to really get the most out of this remote. In a nutshell, an Activity is started by pressing a single button or in this case an icon like "Watch TV" . When you press Watch TV, the TV turns on and switches to the proper input, the Cable box turns on, the receiver turns on and switches to the proper input and output, and finally the 900 becomes a remote for all of those devices at the same time. More on this later.

To get a feel for this device I decided I would first set up all my devices without any activities. Essentially I wanted to just have a remote and be ability to go to one device after the other and see if they worked correctly. At first the software stumped me and didn't appear to let me get past setting up activities. I gave up trying and set some of them up thinking I could always wipe the remote clean and start again. I am not sure where I went wrong but the first activity I set up, "Watch TV" didn't work out so well. The TV didn't turn on, the Cable box turned off, etc. I ran back and forth from my PC to the living room about a dozen times and finally gave up for the night after about 2 hours of head banging. That night I re-read the manual, had the whole next day to ponder and went at it again .

The next morning I deleted all the activities and created them on my own, not using the wizard. I created an Activity, added the devices and then one by one told the software what I wanted each device to do. This was very helpful. I realized this not only got me the expected result, but it made me see how this software and remote really worked. After playing around for about 30 minutes I was able to create several of my most frequent activates. Going back to the equipment I pressed Watch TV. Again the TV did not turn on. If I used the Harmony for that device directly it worked. Back to the PC and set the activity to turn on the TV first. Still no luck. Next I tried the activity and used the on screen help. It asked if the TV turned on, I answered no and presto the TV turned on. After selects "this fixed my problem" on the remote, it worked every time. But; after each change on the PC I had to go through this help processes. I still do not know what the Harmony is doing to correct this.

Once I got all the basic Activities working I found a few other glitches. When I wanted to watch my combo DVF/VCR and use the VCR portion, none of the commands worked. It turns out this device has separate and distinct commands for FF-VCR and FF-DVD. The Harmony set all the DVD commands to that Activity by Default. I simply created two activities, One Watch VHS and one watch DVD even though it's the same source. In fact I found creating different activities for the same source is the answer to everyone complaining about missing the macro feature. It really does the same thing.

Now that I was on a roll my last bit of programming was renaming the activities. If you want the rest of your family to know how to use this thing without a PowerPoint presentation and tutor, I suggest you name the activities in such a way that its very obvious. Examples are Watch TV, Watch Netflix, Use PC, Listen to iPod, Listen to Pandora, etc. Since my receiver has an iPod dock, the Listen to iPod activity changed the source from whatever it is on to the receivers iPod port and then shows all the different music listening modes on the soft buttons. Watch Netflix switches to my Roku, etc.

Now for the best part of the Harmony setup! Its the ability to have the remote on the "Watch TV" activity and being able to program the hard and soft buttons to any other device's remote function. No more switching to the specific device's remote to change an often used setting on that device. If you take your time, you will eventually never have to use the "Devices" soft button as all the things you do will be setup in the Activity you are in. Now this takes some time and trial and error, but it's a huge time saver. Here is an example: You are Watching TV, controlling the sound options and volume with the Receiver, changing channels with the DVR and changing the aspect ration with the TV all on the same keypad. But beware! You can set what buttons do what on the device settings, but that won't change what they do in an Activity. The remote buttons MUST be set up in the Activity to work properly.

I spent several more days fine tuning the remote and now have not touched it in a while. I have a few more tweaks I am thinking of doing. And I would love to find the glitch that makes the TV turn on after I make any updates to the remote. Maybe a call is in order before my 90 days runs out.

USE:

As mentioned above, the ability to have the most common functions for several devices on one remote mode at the same time is huge! Now that I have used it for a couple of weeks, I have gotten accustomed to the button layout and can operate it without looking at it for most basic functions.

When everything is off and you select Watch TV, everything turns on and goes to the right inputs etc. However starting an activity can take quite a while. The remote can not be used while the Activity is being implemented. In my case I am already watching TV with sound on and the remote is still spinning the hour glass for a while. If you have the TV on too loud, you have to wait until the Harmony is done thinking or walk over and turn it down manually. However once that first activity is complete, any subsequent activity is changed fairly quick.

The battery life seems a bit short. I used to change the batteries in my remote once a year. This thing needs to be charged almost every day. If you let it go dead, its time to break out the old remotes during a recharge.

Once set up properly the Harmony 900 is very easy to use and the rest of the family had no problems with it, well almost.

Wife Problems:If your wife, child, etc. has a habit of turning the TV and other equipment on and off manually, you are in for some headaches. Since the Harmony remembers the last state of your devices (if you use it exclusively), it may turn things on instead of off, or off instead of on if someone else manually did that. My wife figured out the remote very quickly they way I have it set up. But she still does a mixture of using the remote and manual power buttons which frustrates both of us. Of course she blames the remote for not working properly when this happens. However anything that takes some blame from me is more than welcome.

RF Setup:

One of my misconceptions about this remote was the boasting of RF (Radio Frequency) capability. IT does indeed have IR capability. However, it does not have a database of RF codes like it does for IR codes. This device will not replace "ANY" RF remote, period. I was hoping there was a RF option for my X-10 home control devices, but that is not the case. For setups like this you need to get a IR to RF converted for the devices you already have. Figuring out which one you need can be a daunting task (See Device Support above).

The only RF device the Harmony will control directly is the IR blaster that comes with the device. An additional IR blaster can also be added. By default the IR blaster emits all the signals the remote puts out through IR to any and all blasters you have set up. You can control which blaster gets which signal. But this can only be done at the remote, not in the software. I am not sure why this is, but it is one of several deficiencies in the software.

Overall:

I went from wanting to return the Harmony 900 within hours of taking it out of the box, to protecting it like it is one of my children. I really love the Harmony 900 and would recommend it to most people. Those with little patients or difficulty working the microwave should avoid it unless someone else can set it up for you. It's overkill on a simply setup, like DVR and TV. But it is a pure joy if you have a medium to complex setup like I do. At $250.00 it is very pricy and hard to justify for a remote. But it seems to solve all my remote issues and to me it's worth it. I give it 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 900 Rechargeable Remote with Color Touch Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTrue Headphones Around-Ear Style, Black Bose is primarily known for their active noise canceling (ANC) phones though they have for years offered non-ANC phones. This is my first pair of Bose phones that are not in the ANC class of headphones and my impression of them is mostly positive. I do see some room for improvement, though.

First off, these are without question the lightest headphones (aside from ear buds) that I have ever worn. I am a bit odd in that I actually prefer heavier headphones but this is strictly a preference, not a criticism. In spite of the weight, the phones fit very nicely and do not feel like they're about to slip off if you lean down. This is not to say they're tight, but they are tight enough to hold well. They're easy to adjust too, so getting them to fit just right is simple enough. If exceptionally lightweight headphones are your thing, this is what you want.

The cord is a little different than other phones I have used in that the jacks on either end are of different sizes. This is good and bad. It's good in that there's no question of how to attach the cord because it only fits one way. But, it also means that a normal cord that comes with practically any other headphone will not work.

The sound quality is definitely better than average but not perfect (certainly not audiophile-level). The sound spectrum seems to be fairly well balanced. The highs are good and the "edges" are crisp and clean for most tracks. The midrange is ok but slightly hollow. The bass is very good without being overdriven. One of the problems with a lot of headphones is that they tend to overdrive the bass which is fine if you really like your bass, but too much can overpower the rest of the spectrum and give some of us headaches. That these phones do not over-amplify the bass is a pleasant surprise.

Having a pair of Bose QC-15 ANC phones, I can compare the two models' sound profiles and there are some slight differences. Where the QC-15s are great at the highs and overdrive the bass, the midrange is sorely lacking. The SoundTrue get the bass right and have good highs but fall slightly short on the midrange (though still better than the QC-15s). Comparing just the sound profiles and ignoring the ANC function, I prefer the SoundTrue over the QC-15s.

The carrying case is nice and should provide some protection when packed for travel. I would have preferred a slightly harder and more crush-resistant case but that's me being picky. There's not a lot of extra room in the case so storage is not really an option with the case.

The price is a little high ($180 as I write this) and that might be a little steep for some. It comes down to whether a less expensive set of phones delivers the same (or better) sound profile.

My overall impression of the Bose SoundTrue headphones is positive. These are very comfortable and exceptionally lightweight and the sound quality is good though not perfect. These phones are above average and are worth consideration if you want non-ANC headphones or if you're looking for very lightweight headphones.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTrue Headphones Around-Ear Style, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Nova Women's Laptop Backpack I walk to school everyday, it's about a 30minute walk. That combined with all the time walking to different buildings once I'm at school, is a lot of time to get cozy with this backpack.

A little back story, I previously owned a unisex North face backpack, I got rid of it because it was too big and hurt my back. I downsized to a women's North face. It was better but it still didn't seem very comfortable and never felt very light even with few items in it.

Cut to this backpack, it's a women's backpack so it's made smaller. (Also I'm 5'7" 120lbs so I'm not terribly small bit still). This backpack feels lighter than others, I think it has to do with the frame, it's very comfortable on. I typically have 2 binders and two medium sized textbooks in my backpack, occasionally I'll bring my laptop. With everything in it, It doesn't irritate my lower back or shoulders after hours of wear.

The backpack also comes with 2 straps on the side that allows you to compress it in even further. When your stuff is closer to your back, and not hanging far out, it's a lot more comfortable. There are several pockets, a large padded pocket for your laptop, another for your books and such and 2 smaller but still very spacious pockets, as well as an interior pocket and nonzippered outer pocket.

The pockets do zip all the way around, but the straps will need to be unbuckled to do this. I'm not gonna lie, I'm very lazy and have not unbuckled the straps since getting this item, (it's been a month), and I've been able to get my books/laptop in and out without a problem.

The pockets for waterbottles are nice and deep so your water bottle won't fall out, and there's also a strap on either side to secure it even further.

The chest strap on this is awesome too. It doesn't compress your chest in an awkward or uncomfortable way which is something I always look for.

The shoulder straps and back are vented so it's been really great for me, a very sweaty person walking in the summer time. Haha

Overall I think this backpack is awesome! I've already recommended it to my school friends, looks like Osprey is my new go to backpack brand!:D
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Nova Women's Laptop Backpack

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown I've had several pairs of Sennheisers before the momentums namely a pair of HD580's from back in 1999 & much more recently a pair of HD650's. Let me start off by saying I'm not an "audiofile" I'm not a headphones snob. I don't name drop as to act like I know everything about all "cans" as they're referred to as. But I do know music & I know MY TYPE of music, which is pretty much everything except Country/Western. I listen 100% through my iphone or iPods.

I come from an LP, then 8 track (yuck), then cassette, then CD background so when I finally went all compressed format I didn't realize what I'd be "missing" I just thought, "Wow what a convenience"!! Anyway, I ended up ditching all my CD's (about 1400 total, originals!) & ripping them into iTunes, total of about 7500 songs. I long ago sold my HD580 back in 2005 & just listened from earbuds. I got tired of these real quick. So I saved up & did my research & just knew I had to have the Senn HD650's but I knew I had to have a good amp so I bought both (used) & I was thoroughly disappointed. I didn't hear this "wide open" expanded 3D imaged sound that everyone bragged about. After "damning" these headphones for being overpriced I realized, after my anger, I was being angry at the wrong item, it wasn't the can's it was the compressed format that removed all the subtle nuances of the original recordings!

So back to the drawing board to look for a decently priced (new) set of headphones. I bought a pair of in ear headphones from Sennhesier of course & these sounded good, better than than the Apple buds. Then I ran into the Momentums! I did my youtube & google research & the Momentums appear to be the one's I've been looking for. It has the controller but are "can" style headphones not earbuds! The cord is just long enough so i can stick my iphone in my pocket but no so long that it'll get caught on a doorknob or something else. The only drawback is it was hard to find the black with red from any type of discount. I got the brown ones reluctantly but I couldn't argue the price I got them for and for what it's worth the brown looks pretty clean & euro with the brushed aluminum.

I knew as soon as I started listening to some of the typical songs I play that I found my pair. They're paired perfectly for the portable MP3, phone or tablet's. You don't need an amp of any kind, they have great sound quality even for a sealed back design an because they're sealed you won't bother anyone sitting next to you at moderate levels. I was kind of put off of how small the ear surroundings were because my ears are not huge but they do stick out a bit, once I found a good position my ears fit fine.

All I can say is that I"m finally happy with a pair of headphones. I think the challenge is to match your style of music with headphones. Don't listen to name droppers & snobs who only talk about Gredo, AKG's HiFiMan & even Sennheisers. People knock Beats by Dre but hey if your music is like 99% current day hip hop & Dance then the Beats are probably the best suited for you. They're not for people who listen to live rock or classical. I had to find that out the hard way those higher priced headphones that require DAC's & AMPS aren't necessarily suited to my music. I believe the momentums are a great "in betweener" set of headphones. For that person who's aged a bit where they're not looking for LOUD & BOOM any more, they know & want detailed sound but they're still at a stage where they're listening to their music in a compressed 256k or less format, mp3 or wave format & not CD's anymore, but want that CD sound brought back.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown

All partitions (4) on the failing drive were copied/cloned to the Samsung drive using an external USB3 enclosure. I then swapped out the failing drive for the Samsung which booted without incident. The 870 definitely tested faster than the old drive, but you cannot really tell the difference in day to day use. USB Multiple Plug Outlet, Unidapt Night Light Outlet with Surge Protector, 3 USB Charging Ports (1 Type C Port), 6 Wide Spaced AC Outlets, Wall Night Light, Fast Charge Multi Plug Extender, White After using surge protection for audio, video and computer equipment for more than 30 years I can definitely say not all of these products are created equally.

While surge protectors will often boast of great protection, more often than not they are more multi outlet plugs rather than actual protection.

I have thoroughly tested this surge protector and it has passed all of my testing. While only rated for 700 joules, this is typically adequate especially when your home has proper grounding. Often similar devices pass my tests initially yet fail after the 1 or 3 month mark - that has not been the case with this item.

The way this is designed allowed me to utilize this in my bathroom to have all of my toiletry accessories charging at once yet have everything compact and tucked away. It’s nice that this doubles as a nightlight that has adjustable levels of light and automatically turns on and off.

The only thing I wish was different was if on the sides the outlets were more widely spaced to allow for larger power blocks - with that being said having 6 outlets should allow most users to have more than enough.

The 3 USB ports are definitely a nice addition as this helps avoid having to use plugs for USB powered devices. There are 2 standard USB-A ports and 1 ultra fast USB-C port.

This is an outstanding surge protector and nightlight that has proven itself through extensive use and testing.

This is definitely a product I recommend.
text_fidelity_b: USB Multiple Plug Outlet, Unidapt Night Light Outlet with Surge Protector, 3 USB Charging Ports (1 Type C Port), 6 Wide Spaced AC Outlets, Wall Night Light, Fast Charge Multi Plug Extender, White

Once I figured that out, I connected the monitor using a spare HDMI cable I had around (they only give you a VGA to VGA cable). The picture quality, even after adjusting brightness, color, warmth, etc. is mediocre. It's dim and a little on the blurry side. Not pleasant to look at.

The base is a bit wobbly and I wouldn't trust this to stay upright if you have a child or large cat around!

The resolution, at 1366x768, makes everything zoomed way in if you're using this with a MacBook Air. As an example, if I click on the Apple menu, the height of the open menu takes up almost half the screen.

I'd be thrilled if I got this at a garage sale for $25 but for $70 on Amazon, it's too expensive for how poor quality it is.

These days, everything seems to have software that you must navigate, and it is seldom as intuitive as it once was for me.

This frame was easy to figure out, though, at least for the features I care about. I skipped right over the parts where it wanted to connect to my network and so forth. I just wanted to upload photos from a micro-SD card, and then have it play them back to me. And it does that very well.

It has a light sensor that adjusts the brightness of the screen automatically if you enable it to, which is a very nice feature that is lacking on my other digital picture frames. I was also able to program it to go to sleep when I'm never up, to save on energy. I didn't want it to be motion activated, as I want it to be displaying photos the moment I walk into the room. Fortunately, this feature is already off by default.

The frame looks really nice, with a small "mat" border around the display. This mat is something that most digital frames are lacking, and let me tell you, this tiny feature makes a huge difference. It really sells the idea that this is a picture frame, instead of merely a digital display. I can't say enough about how much this improves the aesthetic of this frame.

I have a couple of digital frames that I use in a horizontal orientation, so I deleted all my vertical photos from them and moved them onto this one instead, and set it up in a vertical orientation. It is so nice to have the frame matched to the orientation of the photos! You don't get those huge bars on the sides or top/bottom, or if you have it set to crop then you don't crop out 2/3 of the photo!

I have no complaints about this digital photo frame. I can't speak for all of the features, because I have no use for some of them. But the features I wanted work great, and the frame itself looks fantastic!
text_fidelity_b: MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame

My husband bought me these AcousticSheep SleepPhones recently, and what a difference they make! They're very comfortable - okay, the mediums are a little large for me, but I've found a way to position them so they work perfectly. The speakers are thin and pliable, so they're comfortable even if you roll over and lie on them, and the sound is pleasant - not too boomy or too shrill, and you can move the headband so you can listen in both ears or only one, if you prefer.

The one catch is that the wires leading out of the headphones are pretty thin, and judging my previous experience using many headsets and speakers in bed, they're going to break inside at some point. I'd be perfectly happy to replace these once a year as they've improved my quality of sleep (I'm used to waking when I roll onto a hard plastic speaker or earphone).

BTW, the headband itself is sooo soft and comfy - none of the headbands I've used on my hair over the years are this cozy.

Like it said on the package, these truly are pajamas for your ears ;-)

***Update Feb 9, 2014***

It's been just short of a year since I write the above review. Since then, I ordered a second smaller pair of SleepPhones, the band of which wasn't as soft and furry, but it was good for wearing when doing housework. This one didn't come in the same packaging - the packaging was more minimual. My original pair of SleepPhones' wire on the left ear did indeed break, and I bought a third pair. This was in a much smaller package, but was furry and comfy as the first set. Hopefully it will last a bit longer than my original pair - the wires are a bit more robust.

TomTom GO 2535TM World Traveler 5-Inch Bluetooth GPS Navigator with Lifetime Traffic & Maps and Voice Recognition (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The TOMTOM GO2535 TM WTE is quite attractive with a large screen and smooth appearance but because of its size, this is a heavier GPS than many others. A magnetic plug attaches the power supplies either to a computer with its USB plug or to a car with its accessory power plug. As with most GPS devices, no "home" DC power supply is included. I have found the car mount to be great, easy to attach and remove from the windshield with a simple turn. My only complaint with the mount is that it takes some work to direct the device to a visible position and I fear that it will not last as long as the GPS. The magnetic plug slips into a cutout in the mount, allowing it to remain in position so the GPS can quickly be inserted or removed for safekeeping.
As for the functionality of the GPS, it has some problems, thereby preventing me from giving this a 5 star review. I'll simply list the Pros and Cons.
Pros:
Start up time is quick and option to start from last destination can save time if the satellite connection is delayed.
Menu options are easily learned even if at first they seem to include extra steps.
Responds quickly to need for alternate route when a turn is missed.
Ease in moving through functions on screen.
POIs are expansive and easy to discover
Map identifies a location I frequent which is not identified by any other GPS I've used.
Identifies traffic light cameras adequately. Have yet to receive speed camera warning.
Voice commands are intuitive and a little printed card is included if you're in need of prompting.
Connectivity to my Mac is easy and the option to automatically check for updates can save time.

Cons:
Speed is not always accurate. Often has my car going at 10 mph less than actual speed.
When setting a new destination, I've been unable to change the state unless I do it using the voice command. This may be possible, but I haven't had the time to investigate. Since I'm in a metropolitan area and may venture through 2 states and the District of Columbia in less than an hour, it's important for me to access the individual states.
When using phone through the GPS, although I can hear the conversation with no problem, the person on the other end of my call can't hear me clearly. Every time I've used it with a phone, the call has been dropped. I've never had a call dropped otherwise with my phone or other Bluetooth capable device.
Does not recognize voice commands at times.
Voice prompts are very frequent and I'd love to be able to reduce them but not turn it off.
Seldom comes up with the routes I usually take, even with a second try after selecting the Change Route option.

All in all, this is a good GPS navigation device and the lifetime updates are a definite advantage. I haven't traveled the wold with it, but will update my review as necessary with observations internationally. I do know the maps are on the device because I saw them when I performed the update last week and couldn't figure out how to get back to the USA on the device. For some reason, TOMTOM put me in the UK even though I'm registered in the USA and confirmed that selection.

What's interesting is that I still prefer my 3-year-old Navigon for its ease of use, accuracy and lovely displays, with two exceptions. I do not care for their customer service or necessity to download map updates to the device's SD card instead of doing a direct update on a Mac. This TOMTOM excels there and it comes in a very definite second for any GPS I've used. When the time comes for my beloved Navigon to bite the dust, I feel confident that I'll still be happy with this TOMTOM.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom GO 2535TM World Traveler 5-Inch Bluetooth GPS Navigator with Lifetime Traffic & Maps and Voice Recognition (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter This seemed to be the perfect solution to a problem I was having with obtaining Internet access in my basement. The router is located on the upper floor of the house and, while access is fine in every room above ground, access in the basement has been minimal at best.

Installation was very straightforward - just plug one adapter into the router, the other into the wall socket, and plug in whatever device needs access into one of the three plugs located on the wall socket device.

Overall it works pretty well, but is highly sensitive to noise or heavy draws on the power line. For example, I have a dehumidifier in the basement. When that kicks on, I lose the connection. Sometimes it is regained all by itself, but most of the time I have to either reboot (or power cycle) the device that is plugged in, or unplug and then re-plug the adapter. I tried moving the dehumidifier to a different circuit than the one used by the powerline adapter, and also tried plugging the dehumidifier into a surge protector - no difference. So, I make sure the dehumidifier is off before I use any Internet device.

I've had the same issue with other appliances such as certain vacuums - turn them on, and the connection is lost. There have been no problems with appliances operating in other areas of the house, such as the microwave, laser printers, etc. Just happens when you use the appliance in the same room as the powerline adapter.

But, other than these powerline induced interruptions, the device works well. Speedy connection - can't tell any difference between this and any other WiFi connected device. Well worth taking a look at if you have some WiFi dead zones in your house. Just keep an eye out for someone who is about to use a vacuum when you're at a critical spot in the movie you're streaming!
text_fidelity_b: Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord For the price this is a very nice USB microphone, I would agree with other reviewers that it performs on par with or better than similar competing USB condenser mics in this price range such as Blue Snowball or the Behringer C1.

I do wish it came with more accessories though similar to the non-USB version. The Aokeo AK-60 XLR version comes with a scissor boom arm, shock mount and pop filter for the same price.. so if you do happen to have a compatible audio interface with phantom power then I would recommend the XLR version.

The main annoyance with this mic is that when using it in windows 10 the driver does not have native mic gain control option. In many recording programs you can boost the mic gain via other means but if using this mic for gaming or other purposes through the native drivers then you will have to be very close to the mic to produce adequate volume (ie you pretty much need a boom arm) or otherwise you will need to boost gain via external passthrough program such as APO equalizer. I have also tried this mic in linux and the drivers there do have native gain control.

Overall I do think the sound quality and construction of the mic is good for the price and I would recommend it .. just note that if using windows 10 you will probably either need a boom arm or need to use external software to boost the mic gain. A boom arm is strongly recommended anyways to prevent extraneous noises like keyboard clacking, etc..
text_fidelity_b: Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord

LeadsaiL Wireless Computer Mouse, 2.4G Portable Slim Cordless Mouse Less Noise for Laptop Optical Mouse with 4 Buttons, AA Battery Used, USB Mouse for Laptop, Desktop, MacBook Great shape, very much like the classic and ubiquitous Logitech. I like that the pairing device is on-board. Lightweight and simple, a mouse is important for me if needing to get serious work done, especially anything with CAD or Visio.

The big question you need to ask yourself is, do you want a Bluetooth version or one like this that has its own receiver. It seems to me that if you always use this with the same computer and you have Bluetooth built in to the computer, then you probably want Bluetooth. Conversely, if you want this to use with multiple computers and/or you don't have Bluetooth built in to any one of the computers you will use the mouse with, then you'd want something like this. This is because pairing is easier in a case such as this, and drivers usually aren't an issue. Bluetooth usually isn't an issue either, but it might get irritating with frequent changing of machines. At least that is my experience.

Does not come with a carry bag, surprisingly. Mouse roller also functions as a button, as it should. It has an on/off switch on the back, which is nice for saving battery life and being able to leave this hooked up to a permanent install (although with a permanent desk setup, I personally stick with wired).

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I first became enamored of the garmin company after using the one with a rental car. The ease of use and accuracy was impressive. Unfortunately, that model is no longer in production so I opted for this unit.

In general I am pleased. Easy to set up, the unit features a bright, clear screen. It is a snap to use and the directions have been unfailing accurate. I drive alot and so far have used this unit throughout New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, DC and Virginia. I have had no problem with reception even while traversing mountainous regions. I appreciate the advance notice for turns and the voice command system is a convenience.

However, this unit is not flawless. The robotic voice often mispronounces street names and the voice command system seems a bit hard of hearing when it comes to addresses. I have had to pull over and type in the address. The unit does not like to deviate from its chosen route. For instance, one location I frequent in New York is accessible both by the thruway (toll road) and other non-toll main arteries. Both are about the same distance. When I want to avoid the toll route, the unit will recalculate directing that I turn around and follow the initial route multiple times before adjusting to the alternate route. A big deal, no,but annoying nonetheless. While I have not been terribly plagued by the pop ups, they are annoying and potentially unsafe. While the start up guide and manual are adequate, they are barely so. Whatever happened to detailed instructions? But my biggest gripe is the customer service. I called twice with questions and had ridicualously long waits of fifteen minutes and twenty-five minutes respectively. There is no round the clock service. The last time I called it wasnt even available all week, totally unacceptable.

So while I like this system,there is room for improvement.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a: Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th) I would like to give this a five rating but it is still too quirky to receive that. I deducted a star for each major problem-no control over storage and what appears to be an unstable OS. I switched from another android tablet that was giving me problems. My brother has the largest Kindle Fire HD and it looked very nice. I paid extra to get rid of the ads because they were too obtrusive. One would pop in while I was doing something and shut down that app. I wanted a device for reading e-books and listening to audio books. I also wanted something that had external storage that I could manage. Wrong. The app saves to the external storage card but the downloaded content goes directly to the device storage which makes no sense. Why have an external storage option when none of the larger content files will save to it? The sound is more treble than bass, but it sounds good. My device is only 8 GB, so it max'ed out quickly when I downloaded content. I like the thin form factor. This cuts down the amount of weight in my bag. I got the magenta with a purple cover. Maybe it is because this is the first time I am using it, but the OS is very jumpy and the screen is not as responsive as I would like. I have to tap several times to open an app or play a song. Once I figured it out, downloading from my accounts was easy. Unfortunately when I tried to view my internal content, the device went into a loop, then restarted itself and that took a long time. If I ever am able to download to my SD card as the instructions say, then I will be happy to upgrade my review. In the meantime, I am disappointed that this is not able to do what I wanted.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th)
